title: The helper that forgot its rules
scenario:
You lead a 6-person HR team. Last month the team built custom helpers to answer staff questions about leave and onboarding. Some work well; some don't. Your director asks you to fix them before the busy hiring season.

Use the exhibit. The team, helpers and notes are made up for this case. Product facts are from the vendors' help pages in October 2026.
exhibit:
HELPERS (made up)

  1. Claude project "Leave questions"
     Name:         Leave questions
     Description:  Always answer in Spanish. Cite the
                   policy section.
     Instructions: (empty)
     Files:        leave-policy.pdf

  2. Gem "Onboarding buddy" (Gemini app)
     Knowledge:    onboarding-checklist (added from Drive)

  3. Custom GPT "Benefits FAQ" (ChatGPT Enterprise)
     Uses one custom action to look up benefit plans.

TEAM NOTES
  A. Helper 1 answers in English and never cites a section.
  B. In one chat in helper 1, Ana typed the new 2027 leave
     rule. The next day, a new chat didn't know it.
  C. IT will edit the onboarding checklist in Drive next week.
  D. IT says custom GPTs in our workspace are moving to plugins.

questions.prompt: Note A: why does helper 1 ignore the Spanish and citation rules?

options.text: The rules sit in the description, which Claude can't see
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic says Claude will not have access to a project's name and description. Move the rules into the project instructions.

options.text: Projects only follow rules written inside the PDF file itself
options.explanation: Projects have their own instructions field, which applies to every chat. Rules don't need to live in a file.

options.text: Claude projects can't be set to answer in any other language
options.explanation: No page says that. The fix is to put the rule where Claude reads it: the project instructions.

options.text: The rules need to be pasted into every chat to take effect
options.explanation: That is the pasting a project saves you. Project instructions apply to all chats in the project.

questions.prompt: Note B: how do you make every new chat know the 2027 leave rule?

options.text: Ask Ana to repeat the rule in her chat until Claude remembers it
options.explanation: Repeating it in one chat doesn't help other chats. Anthropic says context isn't shared across project chats.

options.text: Rename the project to "Leave questions 2027" so it knows the year
options.explanation: Claude can't see the project name. The name is only a label for people.

options.text: Start every chat in the project with Ana's old chat open beside it
options.explanation: An open chat isn't project knowledge. Only the project's files and instructions reach every chat.

options.text: Add the new rule to the project files, the shared knowledge base
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic: context is not shared across chats in a project unless it is added to the project knowledge base.

questions.prompt: Note C: IT edits the onboarding checklist in Drive. What happens to the Gem?

options.text: It keeps the old copy until someone deletes and rebuilds the Gem
options.explanation: Google says a Gem uses the most recent version of a file added from Drive.

options.text: It uses the new version, since Drive files in a Gem stay current
options.explanation: Right. Google: if you change a file added from Drive, the changes are reflected in your Gem.

options.text: It stops working until the checklist is uploaded from a laptop
options.explanation: No page says that. A Drive file in a Gem's Knowledge follows the latest version.

options.text: It asks every user to approve the new checklist before using it
options.explanation: No page describes such a step. The Gem simply uses the latest Drive version.

questions.prompt: Note D: what should you do before the Benefits FAQ GPT is moved to a plugin?

options.text: Nothing, because the plugin copies the GPT's model and actions
options.explanation: OpenAI says the selected model does not carry over and custom actions must be rebuilt separately.

options.text: Delete the GPT first, so that the plugin can take over its name
options.explanation: No page asks for that. The original GPT becomes read-only after migration; it isn't deleted first.

options.text: Save test prompts, plan the custom action rebuild, then share it
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says to save familiar prompts and one harder case, rebuild custom actions, and share the plugin, which starts private.

options.text: Copy its instructions into a Gem, so no test or rebuild is needed
options.explanation: The custom action that looks up benefit plans must still be rebuilt, and OpenAI says to keep familiar prompts to compare the replacement.
